commands.review_summary:
The branch adds a recent-stale guard to Claude yearless reset date rollover and two StatusProbeTests covering stale same-day reset rendering.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection of current main shows any parsed yearless Claude date-and-time reset in the past is rolled forward by one year, so `Jul 9, 3:00pm` at `2026-07-09 15:05 UTC` becomes a nearly year-long countdown before this PR.

target.title: Fix Claude stale reset rollover
target.body: ## Summary - Keep Claude yearless reset timestamps in the current year when they are only recently stale. - Preserve the existing year-boundary rollover for dates that are far in the past, such as Dec 31 parsing a Jan reset. - Add a regression test for a stale same-day Claude reset that previously became a next-year reset. ## Root cause #1947 correctly fixed yearless Claude reset dates around New Year by rolling past parsed dates into the next year. That rule was too broad for stale same-day reset strings. If Claude still returned an old reset like `Jul 9, 3:00pm` a few minutes after the boundary, CodexBar parsed it as current-year past, rolled it to next year, and the countdown could show roughly `364d 23h`. ## User-visible effect A just-expired Claude reset now renders as `Resets now` until the next refresh replaces the stale snapshot, instead of showing a nearly one-year countdown. ## Verification - `swift test --filter "does not roll stale same day"` - `swift test --filter StatusProbeTests` — 255 tests passed - `git diff --check`
